chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Ali ibn Hadeed from Jamil ibn Darradj said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who has a debt due from another man, and the debtor denies it, so the creditor finds/seizes from his property an amount equal to what was denied. Does he take it, even if the denier does not know about that? He (peace be upon him) said, 'Yes.'

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: There is no contradiction between these narrations because each has its own context. What I say is that if a man has money due from another who denies it, and the creditor makes him swear an oath regarding that, and he swears, then it is not permissible for the creditor to take anything from his property under any circumstance, based on what has been narrated.

key_terms.اسْتَحْلَفَهُ: He made him swear an oath

ai.seo_question: Can a creditor seize a debtor's property if the debtor denies the debt?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the mechanism of *qabd* (seizure) in debt recovery, establishing that a creditor may unilaterally seize assets equal to the denied debt without the debtor's prior knowledge. The accompanying commentary by Muhammad ibn al-Hasan resolves apparent contradictions by distinguishing between simple denial and denial followed by a sworn oath (*yamin*), which serves as a legal bar to further seizure. This highlights the Shia juristic emphasis on the evidentiary weight of oaths in protecting the debtor's property rights.
